"we need more accountability" is often...

...we need more trust
...we need more psychological safety
...we need more support
...we need fewer dependencies
...we need more focus

what else?

OK, this probably deserves some explanation:

PjM:
Schedule? How much? On track? Budget? Requirements? Tasks? Change orders? T&M? Contracts? Delivery risk?

PdM:
Options. Why? Why this? Who? How? Opportunity? Context? Benefits? Market/Competitors? Experiments. Value risk? https://twitter.com/johncutlefish/status/1299889912808837120

if you're working on a project ... hire a great project manager.

Many of the best product managers I know are lousy at project management.
Going to use this as my opening slide for a bit...
imagine if ppl put as much rigor into the "why should we do this" vs. the "when will this be done".
During the pandemic ... a company’s ability to prevent burnout / attrition vs. its competitors is probably more important than anything it can ship.

This is why any roadmap visualized with time on the x axis will fail at conveying certain things (while succeeding at others).

“The roadmap” is one of a 6-12 artifacts necessary for shared understanding. Yet seems to occupy 80% of headspace for PdM https://twitter.com/PavelASamsonov/status/1296818042928861184
Wow. That's a tense WFH gig.

A: [Problem]

B: “Bring me solutions not problems”

A: [Solution]

B: But, but, no, wait, how about..., we should, I’m not sure sure...

A: [More solutions]

B: “What’s the problem again?”

A: [Problem]

If the stuff you’re working on now was “promised” a year + ago ... almost by definition the rest of the org will have moved on mentally and will not be excited about your work.

This is the perpetual disappointment created by large planning batches / low flow.

If you’re going to have a “product triangle” for key decisions (PdM, tech lead, design lead) it really really really really helps if that same structure exists at the highest level, and those people could form a functional product team.
